_comment: Feather segmentation settings (src/feather_processing.py). A Celery task or sample run can override any key with options={'segmentation': {...}} without redeploying. sam3.imgsz needs a worker restart; everything else applies per task. feather_judge = the per-feather checks (score computed from them, see feather_judge.score); inventory = slide-level check for feathers the segmentation may have missed (review flags only, never a new letter or feather ID). The old slide_judge (metadata + a 1-10 overlay score) is retired: the label extractor owns Bird_ID/Date, and the inventory + per-feather checks cover what it asked.

feather_judge.prompt:
You are checking the segmentation of ONE feather on a scanned specimen slide. The image has two panels.
LEFT: the slide around this feather, with the segmentation outline drawn as a thin green line (green lines inside the feather mark holes in the segmentation). Other feathers and the slide background may also be visible.
RIGHT: exactly the pixels inside that outline, on black. Anything black in the RIGHT panel is NOT in the segmentation.

Compare the two panels and answer every check. Judge only what you can see; do not assume anything that is not visible.
When you are unsure about a check, give the answer that flags a problem ("cut", or true; for single_feather, false). A person looks at every flagged feather; a wrong pass is never looked at again.

1. Outline, side by side: for each side of this feather as it appears in the image (left, right, top, bottom), answer "cut" if any visible part of THIS feather (vane, barbs, fringe, tip, shaft or base, including pale, white or translucent parts) extends beyond the green line on that side; otherwise answer "complete". A part hidden under something else on the slide (card, board, tape, another feather) does not count as cut.
2. Holes and gaps: answer true if any part of this feather inside its outline is missing from the RIGHT panel (a hole, gap, notch or band that is black on the RIGHT but feather on the LEFT), or if the segmentation is split into separate pieces. Natural separations between barbs that look the same on both panels are not holes.
3. One feather: single_feather is true only if the outline holds exactly one feather; fragment is true if it holds only a piece of a feather while the rest of that feather is visible outside it.
4. Nothing else: other_feather_inside is true if any part of a different feather is inside the outline, however small. other_material_inside is true if anything that is not feather (slide background, card, board, tape, label, glue, shadow) is inside the outline beyond a thin rim. A thin rim is a band of background that follows the outline and is only a few pixels wide (no wider than about twice the green line). A wider band, or a patch of background anywhere that does not follow the outline, counts as other material.

Answer with JSON only, no other text:
{"outline": {"left": "complete"|"cut", "right": "complete"|"cut", "top": "complete"|"cut", "bottom": "complete"|"cut"}, "holes_or_gaps": true|false, "single_feather": true|false, "fragment": true|false, "other_feather_inside": true|false, "other_material_inside": true|false, "model_score": <1-10: 10 = usable as is for measuring this feather, 1 = unusable>, "notes": "<at most 20 words: which check failed and where, or ok>"}

score._comment: judge_score = start minus each deduction for a failed check (side_cut per side marked cut; holes_or_gaps also when holes or a split mask are measured), at least min. For sorting and summaries only: needs_review, judge_segment_ok and the retry use the checks themselves. The model's own 1-10 answer is stored unused as judge_model_score.

inventory.prompt:
This is a scanned specimen slide with feathers. Every feather that the segmentation found is outlined in colour and labelled with a number in a white box; the numbers run 1, 2, 3 ... from left to right.

1. Count every feather on the slide, whole or partly hidden (under a card, board, tape or another feather). Count only feathers: not labels, text, tape, glue spots or shadows.
2. List every feather that has NO numbered outline. A feather counts as outlined if a numbered outline covers more than half of it. For each one, give the numbers of the outlined feathers directly to its left and right (null if there is none on that side) and its horizontal centre as a fraction of the image width (0 = left edge, 1 = right edge).

When you are unsure whether something is a separate feather or whether it is outlined, list it: a person checks every listed feather, while one you leave out is never looked at. If feathers overlap so much that you cannot tell how many there are, give your best count and say so in notes.

Answer with JSON only, no other text:
{"total_feathers": <integer>, "missed": [{"between": [<number or null>, <number or null>], "x_center": <0-1>, "partly_hidden": true|false}], "notes": "<at most 20 words>"}
Use "missed": [] when every feather is outlined.
